slides.eyebrow: This is why you're still driving to NYC
slides.sub: And a park on the Navesink River is on the same walk. Park once and see all 3.

slides.title: Count Basie Center for the Arts
slides.body: It opened as the Carlton in 1926. It's named for Count Basie, who was born in Red Bank.

slides.title: Riverside Gardens Park
slides.meta: W Front St, on the Navesink
slides.body: A small riverfront park with a boardwalk, a sensory garden and a stage for free shows in season. It's an easy stop between dinner and a show.
slides.source: Borough of Red Bank, redbanknj.org; redbank.org

slides.title: Red Bank Station
slides.body: North Jersey Coast Line trains stop here. The Basie says it's about 3 blocks away, so you can ride in and walk.

slides.title: Red Bank on foot
slides.tip: Walk Monmouth St from the station to the Basie, then head north to the river at W Front St.

caption:
Red Bank is easy to see on foot. Start at the train station, walk Monmouth Street to the Count Basie Center, then head north to the river. Could you see yourself living this close to a show?
